posts.title: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
posts.summary: When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. The more useful the agent becomes, the more calls…
bullets: Agentic coding workflows can consume 10 to 50 times more tokens than standard chat prompts, leading to unsustainable costs that may eventually exceed average developer salaries.
Rationing token usage through blanket caps often restricts high-value workflows; firms should instead measure 'cost per merged pull request' to track actual output efficiency.
Enterprises should implement intelligent routing to reserve expensive frontier models for complex reasoning while offloading routine code generation and testing to lower-cost, open-weight models.

posts.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
posts.summary: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate…
bullets: Less than 50% of agent-generated analytics insights currently lead to actionable business improvements, highlighting a significant gap in ROI for enterprise AI.
The primary driver of substandard output is a lack of business context, suggesting that organizations should prioritize semantic layers and governance over simply scaling model size.
A high-performing cohort of 'insight leaders' achieves a 70% success rate in driving business actions, demonstrating that prescriptive insight quality is a key competitive differentiator.

posts.title: Xpeng to report Q3 results on November 16 after record quarterly deliveries
posts.summary:
Xpeng delivered a record 118,390 vehicles in the third quarter, slightly above the midpoint of its guidance.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xpeng will report its third-quarter 2026 financial results on November 16, following a record quarterly delivery volume of 118,390 vehicles.
Despite strong delivery growth, investors will be focused on whether the company can improve its vehicle margins, which fell to 12.1% in the second quarter.
Management aims to exceed 60,000 monthly deliveries in the fourth quarter, supported by the recent launch of the Mona L05 and G9L models.

posts.title: Chinese automakers reportedly head to Beijing for talks on EU hybrid export quotas
posts.summary:
Several automakers are vying for export allocations under a limited overall quota.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Chinese automakers are negotiating with regulators to secure export allocations for hybrid vehicles to the EU under a new trade understanding.
The proposed framework reportedly sets an initial annual quota of 350,000 hybrid vehicles, with a 6% annual growth rate for four years.
Because the total quota is limited, competition among Chinese manufacturers for these export slots is intensifying, which could significantly impact their European market strategies.

posts.title: Xpeng plans South Korea entry, appoints former Volvo exec to lead local business
posts.summary:
Lee Man-sik will become managing director of Xpeng Korea on December 1, overseeing business development including sales and service networks.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xpeng is expanding into the South Korean market, appointing former Volvo Cars Korea executive Lee Man-sik to lead local operations starting December 1.
The move follows a record-breaking October for Xpeng's international business, which saw 13,326 overseas deliveries.
Overseas expansion has become a vital hedge for Xpeng, with international sales accounting for over 21% of total year-to-date volume.
